answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with stake-aged reputation: a new identity starts with zero trust and earns transaction weight only through peer-attested work that accrues slowly, like a reef building on a lagoon floor. Each identity must also lock a refundable deposit, slashed on fraud, so spawning a thousand fakes means locking a thousand deposits and waiting out the same slow trust ramp for each. Faking one identity is cheap; faking an army able to move value costs capital and time, while honest agents keep their standing — a karst of trust that cannot be counterfeited overnight.
